sanskrit_shloka:
जनक उवाच ॥
अकिञ्चनभवं स्वास्थ्यं कौपीनत्वेऽपि दुर्लभम् ।
त्यागादाने विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥ १३-१॥
translation: Janaka said: Even in the state of possessing nothing, inner well-being is hard to attain, though one have only a loincloth. Having abandoned both renunciation and acquisition, I sit happily, as I please.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Janaka said: Even in the state of possessing nothing, inner well-being is hard to attain, though one have only a loincloth. Having abandoned both renunciation and acquisition, I sit happily, as I please.

commentary_faqs.question: What is the significance of the 'loincloth' reference in Verse 1?
commentary_faqs.answer: Janaka points out that external signs of renunciation, like wearing only a loincloth, do not guarantee inner peace if the mind is still caught in the duality of accepting and rejecting.

commentary_faqs.question: How does Janaka handle daily activities like walking or sleeping?
commentary_faqs.answer: He views them as natural bodily functions that do not affect his inner state of happiness, as he has abandoned the sense of being the 'doer' of these actions.

sanskrit_shloka:
कुत्रापि खेदः कायस्य जिह्वा कुत्रापि खिद्यते ।
मनः कुत्रापि तत्त्यक्त्वा पुरुषार्थे स्थितः सुखम् ॥ १३-२॥
translation: Somewhere the body grows weary, somewhere the tongue becomes fatigued, and somewhere the mind too tires. Abandoning all this, I remain happily established in the supreme human aim.

sanskrit_shloka:
कृतं किमपि नैव स्याद् इति सञ्चिन्त्य तत्त्वतः ।
यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत् कृत्वासे यथासुखम् ॥ १३-३॥
translation: Knowing in truth that nothing whatsoever need be done, when something comes to be done, I do it and remain happily, as I please.

sanskrit_shloka:
अर्थानर्थौ न मे स्थित्या गत्या न शयनेन वा ।
तिष्ठन् गच्छन् स्वपन् तस्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥ १३-५॥
translation: Gain and no-gain do not concern me by standing, walking, or lying down. Therefore, whether standing, walking, or sleeping, I remain happily, as I please.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वपतो नास्ति मे हानिः सिद्धिर्यत्नवतो न वा ।
नाशोल्लासौ विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥ १३-६॥
translation: For me there is no loss in sleeping, nor attainment through striving. Abandoning both decline and elation, I remain happily, as I please.

sanskrit_shloka:
सुखादिरूपा नियमं भावेष्वालोक्य भूरिशः ।
शुभाशुभे विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥ १३-७॥
translation: Having often observed in the states of being the fluctuations of happiness and other moods, and having abandoned both the auspicious and the inauspicious, I abide as I please, in bliss.
